facts.fact_text: A demonstration was planned to be held in Baku on 12 January 2013.
A demonstration was planned to be held in Baku on 26 January 2013.
A demonstration was planned to be held in Baku on 10 March 2013.
According to the applicants, the demonstrations were intended to be peaceful.
According to the applicants, the demonstrations were conducted in a peaceful manner.
The demonstration of 12 January 2013 was aimed at protesting about the deaths of soldiers in the army.
The demonstration of 10 March 2013 was aimed at protesting about the deaths of soldiers in the army.
The demonstration of 26 January 2013 condemned the use of force by the police against the participants of previous demonstrations.
Each applicant attended one of the demonstrations (as specified in the Appendix).
Shortly after the demonstrations had begun, the police started to disperse those who had gathered.
All three applicants were arrested during the dispersal operations.
All three applicants were taken to police stations following their arrest.
On the day of each applicant's arrest, administrative-offence reports (inzibati xəta haqqında protokol) were issued.
The administrative-offence reports stated that the applicants had committed an administrative offence under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The first-instance courts found that the applicants had participated in unauthorised demonstrations.
The applicants were convicted under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The applicants were sentenced to fines of 450, 500 and 600 Azerbaijani manats respectively (as specified in the Appendix).
At the time of the applicants' arrest, Article 5 § IV of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that no prior written notification was required for spontaneous assemblies.

Before amendments were introduced by Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012, a breach of the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies had been punishable under Article 298 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 2000 by a reprimand or a fine of between 7 and 13 Azerbaijani manats.
Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012 entered into force on 1 January 2013.
Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012 introduced new wording to Article 298 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 2000 on breaching the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies.

Under the amendment introduced by Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012, participation in an assembly organised in breach of the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies became explicitly punishable under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 2000.

Under the amendment introduced by Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012, administrative detention of up to fifteen days was introduced as a punishment for participation in an assembly organised in breach of the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies.

Under the amendment introduced by Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012, community service was introduced as a punishment for participation in an assembly organised in breach of the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies.

Under the amendment introduced by Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012, the fine for a breach of the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies was increased to between 300 and 600 Azerbaijani manats for participants of an assembly.

Under the amendment introduced by Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012, the fine for a breach of the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies was set at between 1,500 and 3,000 Azerbaijani manats for individuals who organise an assembly.

Under the amendment introduced by Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012, the fine for a breach of the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies was set at between 3,000 and 6,000 Azerbaijani manats for persons in charge (vəzifəli şəxslər) who organise an assembly.

Under the amendment introduced by Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012, the fine for a breach of the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies was set at between 15,000 and 30,000 Azerbaijani manats for legal entities involved in the organisation of an assembly.

Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe, entitled 'The honouring of obligations and commitments by Azerbaijan', noted that there is no political dialogue with the opposition parties outside parliament in Azerbaijan.

Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe expressed concern about the restrictive climate for the activities of the extra-parliamentary opposition in Azerbaijan, which complains about limitations imposed on freedom of expression and freedom of assembly and the lack of access to the public media.

Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe stated that the establishment of an inclusive political system and a truly competitive and unrestrictive political environment requires full implementation of basic freedoms, including freedom of expression, freedom of assembly and freedom of association.
Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe expressed deep concern about the situation regarding basic freedoms in Azerbaijan.

Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe expressed concern about recently adopted amendments to the Criminal Code and the Administrative Code of Azerbaijan, which increased penalties for the organisers of, and participants in, 'unauthorised' gatherings.

Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe noted that, considering the authorities' ongoing blanket ban on protests in the Baku city centre, the amendments to the Criminal Code and the Administrative Code were likely to have a further negative impact on freedom of assembly and freedom of expression.

Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe expressed concern about the restrictive use of certain articles of the Criminal Code of Azerbaijan, in particular Articles 221 and 233, against participants in peaceful, albeit unauthorised, demonstrations.
The Report (CommDH(2013)14) of 6 August 2013 was produced by Nils Muižnieks, the Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe, following his visit to Azerbaijan from 22 to 24 May 2013.

The Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe, Nils Muižnieks, expressed deep concern in his Report (CommDH(2013)14) of 6 August 2013 about recent amendments to the Law on Freedom of Assembly, the Criminal Code and the Code of Administrative Offences of Azerbaijan, which further erode the right to freedom of assembly.

The Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe, Nils Muižnieks, stated in his Report (CommDH(2013)14) of 6 August 2013 that the sanctions which can now be imposed, coupled with the fact that local authorities have not authorised a single rally in Baku city centre in recent years, clearly have a chilling effect on the organisation of or participation in demonstrations.

The Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe, Nils Muižnieks, stated in his Report (CommDH(2013)14) of 6 August 2013 that participants in peaceful assemblies should not be sanctioned for the mere fact of being present at and actively participating in the demonstration in question, provided they do not do anything illegal, violent or obscene in the course of it.

The Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe, Nils Muižnieks, urged the Azerbaijani authorities in his Report (CommDH(2013)14) of 6 August 2013 to ensure that no disproportionate sanction, which would undermine the fundamental right to peaceful assembly, is imposed.
